description: Draw a plugin's editor to a PNG, after a test signal plays through it. Give plugin (an id) or script (a name in the library). Then the editor is drawn without a window, scale times its design size, and saved as a PNG (path; width and height in pixels): read the file to see it. A script with neither editor() nor draw() shows the automatic editor. pointer, if given, acts on the editor first, in its design units (the picture's pixels at scale 1): move (a hover; a drag after a press), press, release, click, double_click, drag (from x, y to to_x, to_y) and wheel (steps notches, up positive), with shift, ctrl or alt held; edits is a merge patch of what they changed, as a user's edits would. problems says what went wrong in the editor's code (a loop stopped by its budget, an index out of range), with the line. Headless pictures use EGL on Linux, Metal on macOS and WGL on Windows; an unavailable renderer returns dsp.no_picture. See describe for errors and examples.

name: dsp_test
title: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch.
description: Play test signals or notes through a plugin and measure it: levels, THD, pitch. Give plugin (an id: a script's, or any effect's or instrument's) or script (a name in the library). A fresh instance, set by patch (a merge patch) when given, plays each signal. An effect: sine (frequency_hz; gain_db and thd_percent), sweep (20 Hz to 20 kHz), impulse (response_db at octave centres), pink noise and silence, each peaking at level_db; and file, audio_file played as it is (resampled to the render's rate, mono on both channels, at most 60 s), the only signal when signals is not given. An instrument, at velocity 0.8: notes (a note, then a chord), note (A4; pitch_hz, the pitch heard), and silence (no notes); release_ms is how long the sound lasts after the last release. Each reports peak and RMS in dBFS, DC, samples beyond 0 dBFS and denormals; problems says in words what looks wrong (clipping, DC, sound from silence, no output, a note out of tune, sound that never dies away, non-finite samples the framework silenced, a script stopped by its loop budget or indexing outside an array). cpu_percent is measured, so it varies between runs. save: true keeps each output as a WAV (path) for analyze and compare. automation is a list of {param, at_s, value}: semantic patch keys and physical values, as discrete sample-accurate changes applied to every signal (no implicit ramps). automation.max_step is the largest adjacent-sample change in full-scale amplitude; baseline_max_step uses the same render without automation; excess_step is their positive difference. A step above both four times baseline and 0.05 suggests clicks or zipper noise: a screening heuristic, not proof of an artifact or of inaudibility. sidechain supplies a timed key; its middle half is measured against a connected silent key with identical automation: gain_change_db is negative for ducking, null if either output is below -120 dBFS. Slow attack may not settle in that window. Each pass has a fresh instance and initial patch. THD and impulse response are omitted during automation or a non-silent key; gain_db then describes the changing render, not static gain. notes supplies an instrument's sequence ({key, velocity, start_s, length_s}), replacing the notes signal; defaults become notes and silence. Do not combine it with the A4 note signal or select only silence. release_ms starts at its last note-off. Times round to samples at the render rate; spans must fit within seconds. sample_rate renders at that rate instead of the session's (sandbox) or the project's (DAW); latency is in samples at the rate used, which sample_rate in the result reports. meters gives a semantic plugin's read-only parameters (its meters and readouts) by patch key in physical units, as they stood when the signal ended (the tail after it does not move them). traces gives what a script's trace(name, value) calls recorded over the signal, in trace_points intervals of trace_interval_s: for each name, the last value in each interval and the lowest and highest, null where none was given. See describe for errors and examples.

description: List native audio device names, host APIs, rates and channel capacities. Enumerates PortAudio devices on macOS/Windows without opening a stream. backend defaults to portaudio; dummy returns an empty list without initializing hardware. Use exact host_api and name values with engine.start. Linux uses JACK ports and returns backend.unsupported; engine.inputs lists running JACK inputs. See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_inputs
title: The device's audio inputs, MIDI devices and the outputs masters play to.
description: The device's audio inputs, MIDI devices and the outputs masters play to. audio: one entry per input channel (channel, the 1-based number track.set record_input takes, and the device port it is connected to). midi: the MIDI devices (names track.set record_midi matches; JACK ports or native CoreMIDI/WinMM inputs, fixed until restart). outputs: one entry per output channel (channel, the number track.set hw_output takes for a master, and the port it is connected to). While the engine is stopped: running false and empty lists (engine.start opens the device). See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_start
title: Start playback through JACK, native PortAudio, or a device-free dummy.
description: Start playback through JACK, native PortAudio, or a device-free dummy. backend: jack (Linux default), portaudio (macOS/Windows native device), or dummy (default elsewhere, no device). For portaudio, host_api, input_device and output_device select exact names from engine.devices. inputs defaults to 0 (playback only); outputs (the device channels masters can play to, track.set hw_output) defaults to one per physical playback port with JACK (2 to 64) and 2 otherwise. rate defaults to the project rate; a rate given is asked of the device (CoreAudio switches the device's rate when it can, WASAPI converts) or, with JACK on PipeWire, suggested to the graph (node.rate: applied only while the devices are idle and the rate is allowed). force_graph (JACK on PipeWire, default false) instead forces block as the graph's quantum, and rate if given, while the engine runs. PortAudio opens up to 16 native MIDI inputs; engine.inputs lists their names. Dummy is paced like a device. block: the device block in frames (default 256); the device's period may differ and is reported. anticipative (default true): render ahead of the playhead on worker threads (edits are heard up to 200 ms later); false renders everything in the audio callback. The engine runs at the device's rate (media is resampled; renders stay at the project's rate). Background and live thread capacities follows the app's Audio processing threads preference (Automatic by default); live helpers join each callback with no added latency. memory_lock reports the default-off host-process memory policy: requested, active, and a structured OS error on failure. cpu_idle_latency reports the default-off 20 microsecond PM QoS request, released on engine stop. A protection failure does not prevent audio startup. MIDI inputs that refuse to open are skipped: midi_warnings reports each device, numeric os_error, message and corrective hint; audio continues. See describe for errors and examples.

name: engine_status
title: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns.
description: Real-time engine state: backend, rate, block, device period, latency, xruns. preparing_audio: source preparation is pending; the previous ready plan stays audible. prepared_version is the last compiled version, preparation_version the pending target (zero when idle); preparation_error explains a failed preparation. plan_latency: the session's plugin delay in frames; device_latency: frames from the engine's outputs to the device. restart_needed: the device changed rate or went away; engine.stop and engine.start again. midi_devices_changed is advisory: MIDI topology changed but audio keeps running. midi_devices_message asks for an explicit engine restart to pick up the new set; existing port names stay fixed. midi_dropped: native MIDI messages/packets rejected or lost to bounded queues (zero for other backends). midi_warnings lists inputs skipped at start, with device, numeric os_error, message and corrective hint. meter_drops: entries a full ring dropped (the renderer's, the audio callback's) — a strip's peak/RMS missed a block, never audio. dropped/voice_dropped count lost plug-in output/voice records. memory_lock reports requested/active and an optional OS error with errno and a corrective hint, including while stopped. Bridges are excluded. cpu_idle_latency reports the owned 20 microsecond request with the same status/error fields; it affects system idle while held and leaves CPU frequency policy unchanged. live_helpers is the enabled live helper capacity. scheduling: each thread class's policy (none, normal, fifo, rr, high) and priority as applied at start: the device callback, live helpers, renderer and background helpers (real-time below a real-time callback when permitted). workgroup: whether the live helpers joined the device's audio workgroup (macOS CoreAudio; state none, ready, joined, partial or failed, with the helper counts and the last refusal's OS error, message and hint). warnings includes scheduling fallbacks and plan warnings with corrective actions. failed_errors adds structured code, message, path and hint to each failure. failed_fx: isolated plugins whose process crashed or hung (silent now; fx.restart re-creates them). See describe for errors and examples.

name: env_add
title: Automate a parameter: a track's or route's mixer control, or a plugin's.
description: Automate a parameter: a track's or route's mixer control, or a plugin's. Target one of track (param volume|pan|mute; playrate only on tr_0), route (volume|pan|mute), group (VCA volume|mute), or fx (a semantic key such as "gain" or "filter1.cutoff", or for other plugins a CLAP id or parameter name), or module (a rack module's knob by key, values in its unit, a choice by its key; module.describe). points: [{beat|bar|seconds, value, shape?, tension?}]; values in the parameter's unit (dB, %, Hz… — text like "800 Hz" works for plugins); shapes linear, square, slow, fast_start, fast_end, bezier. Plugin values move along the parameter's curve (a log cutoff sweeps evenly in pitch). take (param volume|pan|mute): a take envelope, its points in beats from the item's start (it moves with the item); it shapes the take after its take FX (a MIDI take needs an instrument in its take FX). Master playrate points are finite numeric ratios 0.25..4.0; an active nonempty master curve replaces the saved scalar during playback and rendering. Audio sources convert before take FX/live mixing; MIDI and automation follow the same timeline clock. See describe for errors and examples.

description: Set semantic parameters in units, or plain plugin parameters by name/id. Plain CLAP/VST3 values use the declared range or plugin text; read-only parameters refuse edits. See describe for errors and examples.

inactive.description: Params set that do not apply with the new values: kept, and heard once what fx.describe full's active_when names allows it

name: fx_patch_get

description: Read a semantic plugin's saved patch.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_list
title: List an instance's read-only factory patches, by name.
description: List an instance's read-only factory patches, by name.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_patch_merge

description: Merge a partial patch into a plugin instance; returns the effective change. Semantic plugins only. Values in physical units: {"params": {"gain": "-6 dB"}}. See describe for errors and examples.

inactive.description: Params set that do not apply with the new values: kept, and heard once what fx.describe full's active_when names allows it

name: fx_patch_set
title: Replace a semantic patch, or apply a factory patch by name.
description: Replace a semantic patch, or apply a factory patch by name. Give exactly one of patch or name. Factory names come from fx.patch.list; omitted parameters take defaults. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_preset_delete
title: Delete one of the user's presets for a plugin; factory presets stay.
description: Delete one of the user's presets for a plugin; factory presets stay. Removes the user preset's file. Factory presets belong to the plugin and cannot be deleted. Instances that loaded the preset keep their settings. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_preset_list
title: List a plugin's presets: its factory ones, then the user's.
description: List a plugin's presets: its factory ones, then the user's. source factory: the plugin's own patches in its order (read-only; the same as fx.patch.list's names). source user: the user's saved presets for this plugin, sorted by name, with their file path. See fx.preset.load and fx.preset.save. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_preset_load
title: Apply a factory or user preset to a plugin instance in one undo step.
description: Apply a factory or user preset to a plugin instance in one undo step. name from fx.preset.list. source (factory or user) is needed only when both have the name. A factory preset or a semantic plugin's user preset replaces the whole patch (omitted parameters take defaults); a plain plugin's user preset is its saved state. Options such as wet and bypass are not part of a preset. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_preset_save
title: Save a plugin instance's current settings as a named user preset.
description: Save a plugin instance's current settings as a named user preset. Saves what the running plugin has now (editor edits included): the patch of a semantic plugin, else its state. The preset is the user's, for every instance of this plugin in any project. A factory preset's name cannot be taken; replace: true overwrites a user preset of that name. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_remove
title: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes).
description: Remove a plugin instance (and its envelopes).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_restart
title: Re-create a plugin instance from its saved patch/state (after a crash).
description: Re-create a plugin instance from its saved patch/state (after a crash). engine.status lists failed_fx: isolated plugins whose process crashed or hung. The new instance starts from the model's patch or state. See describe for errors and examples.

name: fx_set
title: Set instance options: bypass, offline, wet (%), label, isolation, pins.
description: Set instance options: bypass, offline, wet (%), label, isolation, pins. isolation: in_process, dedicated (the plugin runs in a process of its own: a crash silences only it), shared_bridge (one process for all such plugins), inherit (the project default: in_process). pins: which of the track's channels (1-based; track.set channels adds 3-128) the plugin reads ({in: [l, r]}), writes ({out: [l, r]}) and keys from ({key: [3, 4]}: a detector on 3/4, for a plugin with a sidechain input); {} restores 1/2 in and out. out past its first two entries: a track channel for each of the plugin's auxiliary output channels in order (0: unconnected); fx.add sets them for a multi-out instrument. See describe for errors and examples.

wet.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (%; accepts quantity strings)

name: group_add
title: Create a named track group with optional links and members.
description: Create a named track group with optional links and members.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: group_describe
title: Describe a track group's membership, links and VCA ancestry.
description: Describe a track group's membership, links and VCA ancestry.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: group_list
title: List track groups, linked attributes and optional VCA controls.

name: group_members_set
title: Replace a group's track membership; an empty array clears it.
description: Replace a group's track membership; an empty array clears it.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: group_remove
title: Remove a track group and its VCA, keeping its tracks.
description: Remove a track group and its VCA, keeping its tracks.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: group_set
title: Change a group's name, color, links or active state.

title: Resolve linked tracks or matching items for an edit or selection.
description: Resolve linked tracks or matching items for an edit or selection.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_list

description: List the current branch's recent versions (newest first).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_redo
title: Redo the last undone change.
description: Redo the last undone change.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: history_undo
title: Undo the last change on the current branch.
description: Undo the last change on the current branch.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_add
title: Add an item on a track: MIDI in notation, a MIDI file or an audio file.
description: Add an item on a track: MIDI in notation, a MIDI file or an audio file. position in beats (quarter notes from the start) or bar (1-based). notation: e.g. "voice bass; 1: C2:q r:q C2:q r:q | F2:h G2:h" — every bar must add up; the item is as long as the written bars unless length (beats) is given. audio_file: a path at the project's sample rate; with the app's copy-imports setting on, the project keeps its own copy in its media folder. midi_file: a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or 1, every track merged, channels kept); its notes keep their beats and follow the project's tempo (the file's tempo and meter are not applied; a warning says when they differ), and the item is as long as the file unless length is given. A master holds audio items only (prints, played after its fader); busses hold none. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_apply-fx
title: Render an item through its take and track FX into a new audio take.
description: Render an item through its take and track FX into a new audio take. Renders the heard take alone (other items on the track silent) through its take FX and the track's main chain, before the fader and pan, over the item's span: MIDI becomes audio through the track's instrument. The file goes to the project's media folder. mode take: a new take, heard, beside the old one (MIDI stays a take). mode replace: the new take takes the old one's place. The item's fades and gain still apply when it plays; the track FX still process the result, so bypass or move them if they should not apply twice. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_consolidate
title: Consolidate selected audio and MIDI per track in a background job.
description: Consolidate selected audio and MIDI per track in a background job. Partitions by track and active source kind. Audio bakes active takes, item controls, warp and take FX/automation to float WAV; track processing remains live. MIDI items on a track become one item (each item's heard take, gaps empty, overlaps layered); a lone MIDI item with several MIDI takes layers them into one take; other lone MIDI stays unchanged. Select complete linked/warp bundles on matching lanes/groups. One undo step after successful job publication. No item-count cap; existing render/source sample budgets apply. job.get returns resulting items/files. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_duplicate
title: Copy an item and its takes to a new beat position (default: immediately after).
description: Copy an item and its takes to a new beat position (default: immediately after).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_explode-takes
title: Spread an item's takes onto new tracks, or one after another on its track.
description: Spread an item's takes onto new tracks, or one after another on its track. In recording order. mode tracks: the first take stays on the item's track and each other take gets a new channel right below it (named after the take) at the same time. mode serial: the takes follow each other on the item's own track, each as long as the item. Every take becomes a one-take item with its FX and envelopes. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_export
title: Write an item's raw audio (WAV) or its MIDI (SMF) to a file.
description: Write an item's raw audio (WAV) or its MIDI (SMF) to a file. Exports the active take over the part the item covers (trims and splits respected). Audio: the source's own samples, rate and channels, from the source position at the item's start to the one at its end (playrate, unpreserved pitch and stretch markers decide that span but are not applied; a looping item ignores markers and repeats its source as heard; outside the source is silence). No gain, fades, pan, channel mode, FX or track processing. 16/24-bit PCM WAV sources keep their format; others are 32-bit float. MIDI: what the item plays (loops unrolled, notes ending by its end) from 0, at the source PPQ, with the tempo and meter at the item's start. Relative paths resolve against the work directory; a missing extension is added; existing files are replaced, the project's media never. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_heal
title: Heal compatible consecutive audio pieces without rendering.
description: Heal compatible consecutive audio pieces without rendering. One chain per track, complete linked/warp selection, matching stored audio/take/FX properties and continuous source maps. Accepts touching split pieces and unchanged linear Slice-at-hits overlaps up to 50 ms. Keep all left takes, outer fades and full warp maps; remove interior slice fades. Nonlinear envelope seams that cannot be recovered refuse. Stored FX states must match exactly; no live plugin queries or audio rendering. One undo step. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_mix-to-track
title: Mix the selected items through their strips onto a new muted channel.
description: Mix the selected items through their strips onto a new muted channel. Background job. Only the given items sound; each plays through its channel's full strip (take FX, item gain/fades, track FX, automation, fader, pan, Console 9 encode), and the sum is decoded by a neutral Console 9 Buss, as a fresh buss fed by those channels hears it. Sends, parent busses, mute switches and solo are ignored. Span: earliest item start to latest end, no tail. Result: a project-rate stereo float WAV in the media folder on a new muted channel after the last source (under their common parent, else the main master), one item at the span's start. Source items stay. One undo step; job.get returns track, item and file. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_move
title: Move an item in time (position in beats or bar) and/or to another track.
description: Move an item in time (position in beats or bar) and/or to another track.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_paste
title: Copy items as they were in a version (a clipboard) to tracks and beats.
description: Copy items as they were in a version (a clipboard) to tracks and beats. version: where the items are read (default: now) — a GUI copy or cut remembers the version, so a paste reproduces the items as copied even after they were removed or edited. items: [{item, track, position}] (beats; channels only). Takes, fades, take FX and MIDI are copied; an audio source the project no longer has is restored. See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_remove
title: Remove an item with its takes (unpooled sources go too).
description: Remove an item with its takes (unpooled sources go too).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: item_set
title: Set an item's position, length, playback, fades, name, color, or lock.
description: Set an item's position, length, playback, fades, name, color, or lock. Positions and lengths are in beats; fades are in seconds. Name is the active take's name. A locked item refuses every edit except {"locked": false}. timebase: what the item follows when the tempo changes — beats (moves and stretches with it), time (stays at its seconds), beats_position (its start follows the beat, its length stays in seconds) or track (inherit); the item keeps its place now. See describe for errors and examples.

locked.description: The arrange view marks locked items.

gain_db.description: Quantity strings are range-checked by the server. (dB; accepts quantity strings)

name: item_split
title: Split an item at a beat, optionally at the prior audio zero crossing.
description: Split an item at a beat, optionally at the prior audio zero crossing. snap defaults to none. zero_crossing searches the active take's prepared playback source up to 100 ms before at, before FX/fades/gain. After channel mode, use the louder stereo channel by window energy (left on ties), never a stereo sum unless MonoMix is selected. Choose the latest exact zero or sign-change sample boundary; never search forward or outside the item. Without a crossing, split at at. MIDI and empty takes refuse zero_crossing; the GUI skips them. Current prepared audio must be available; start the engine and retry after preparation. Linked items use the initiating item's resolved split time. History records that time for replay. See describe for errors and examples.

name: log_list
title: Recent commands with origin, arguments and outcome (the command log).
description: Recent commands with origin, arguments and outcome (the command log). Newest last. Who did what: origin is gui, agent:<client>/<model>, mcp:<client>, lua:<script>, rpc. queries: include read-only commands (left out by default). since: only entries after this seq (poll with the last seq seen). origin: entries whose origin starts with this. The log keeps the last 2000 commands. See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_add
title: Add a named marker in beats.
description: Add a named marker in beats.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_list
title: List rulers in this project.
description: List rulers in this project.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_remove
title: Remove a ruler.
description: Remove a ruler.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: marker_set
title: Edit a ruler's position, name, or color.
description: Edit a ruler's position, name, or color.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_edit
title: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize.
description: Edit a MIDI item's notes and CCs: add, remove, move, resize, velocity, quantize. ops run in order and are one undo step. notes: indices into midi.notes' list as it was before this command (every op refers to that list, so later ops are not affected by earlier removals). Beats are from the item's start. add {pitch, start, length, velocity?, channel?}; remove {notes}; move {notes, beats?, semitones?}; resize {notes, length? | length_delta? | start_delta?}; velocity {notes, velocity? and/or velocity_delta?}; quantize {notes? (all), grid (beats, on the project's grid), strength? 0-1, ends?}; cc.set {number, points [{beat, value}], channel?}; cc.clear {number, from?, to?}. Returns the new indices of the notes the ops added or changed (to keep a selection). See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_get
title: Read an item's MIDI as notation.
description: Read an item's MIDI as notation.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_notes
title: List a MIDI item's notes and CC points (beats from the item's start).
description: List a MIDI item's notes and CC points (beats from the item's start). Notes are in a fixed order (by start, then pitch); midi.edit refers to them by their position in this list. start/length/beat are in beats from the item's start; channel is 1-16 (omitted for 1). pooled: other items share this MIDI, and edits change them too. For writing whole phrases, midi.write with notation is usually better. See describe for errors and examples.

name: midi_write
title: Replace an item's MIDI with notation (the item keeps its position and length).
description: Replace an item's MIDI with notation (the item keeps its position and length).  See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_add
title: Add a module to a rack: a type with knob values.
description: Add a module to a rack: a type with knob values. type: an id or a short name ("vca", "notes"; module.list). x, y: its top-left corner in the rack (default: right of the others). params: knob values by key in the knob's units (a choice by its key, a switch as a bool). Notes: source (the track whose MIDI it plays; default the rack's channel) and device (a live MIDI input it always plays; "" any). plugin (instead of type): a plug-in id (fx.scan) for a plugin module, which shows the plug-in's name and opens its editor; its ports are in_l, in_r, out_l, out_r and, for instruments, pitch, gate and velocity. preset: a factory preset (module.describe), params on top. Returns its size and keys. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_check
title: Compile a module without saving it; return its diagnostics and description.
description: Compile a module without saving it; return its diagnostics and description. source (a whole module) or name (one in the library). ok is true when it compiles; type then describes it as module.describe would. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_describe
title: A module type's knobs, inputs and outputs, with units and help.
description: A module type's knobs, inputs and outputs, with units and help. type (an id or a short name, "vca") or module (a module's type). Knobs: key, name, kind (number, integer, choice, toggle), unit, min, max, default, choices (keys), group, help. Ports: key, name, signal (audio, pitch in octaves from C4, gate, cv -1..1, unipolar 0..1, phase 0..1), help, and an input's normal (its value with nothing connected). A cable into a knob moves it by amount per unit of signal: octaves for a frequency, the knob's own unit otherwise. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_duplicate
title: Duplicate modules, with the cables between them.
description: Duplicate modules, with the cables between them. The copies sit dx, dy from the originals (default 0, 40 below the lowest). cables (default true): cables among the given modules are copied too. Plugin modules copy their plug-in with its state. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_edit
title: Edit a library module in place: replace text, then save and compile it.
description: Edit a library module in place: replace text, then save and compile it. name (or type, a library module's id). Each edit replaces old, which must be in the source exactly once, with new (empty deletes it), in order and all or none. Then as module.write: saved, compiled, and racks playing it rebuilt. See describe for errors and examples.

old.description: text the source has in one place

name: module_fork
title: Copy a module type's source into the library under a new id.
description: Copy a module type's source into the library under a new id. type: the one to copy (stock or library). id: the copy's ("com.<you>.<name>"). name: its library name (default: the id's last part). The copy is saved and compiled as module.write does; then module.edit changes it. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_get
title: A module type's source: stock or library.
description: A module type's source: stock or library. type (an id or short name: every stock module's source is readable, a good start for your own) or name (a library module's file, also when it does not compile). See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_learn_list
title: List the MIDI controllers of module knobs.
description: List the MIDI controllers of module knobs. Every module's, or one module's. control names the message in words. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_learn_remove
title: Remove a module knob's MIDI controller.
description: Remove a module knob's MIDI controller.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_learn_set
title: Let a MIDI controller turn a module's knob.
description: Let a MIDI controller turn a module's knob. One binding per knob (a new one replaces it). midi.device: a substring of the MIDI input's name (empty: any). mode for a CC: absolute, relative1 (127 = -1, 1 = +1), relative2 (63 = -1, 65 = +1), relative3 (65 = -1, 1 = +1) or toggle. soft_takeover: an absolute control acts once it reaches the knob. A knob turns along its travel (a frequency's is logarithmic); each movement is one undo step. A plugin module's knobs are its plug-in's: fx.learn.set. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_list
title: List module types: id, name, tags, what they do.
description: List module types: id, name, tags, what they do. Host modules (Out, In, Notes, Transport) first, then stock, the user's library and the project's. query matches names, ids, tags and descriptions; tag one tag. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_randomize
title: Move a module's knobs at random, by an amount.
description: Move a module's knobs at random, by an amount. amount 0..1 (default 0.25): how far each knob may move, as a share of its range (choices change with that probability); switches stay. seed makes it repeatable. Returns the knobs it set. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_remove
title: Remove a module with its cables.
description: Remove a module with its cables. Also its knob envelopes; an Out module's channels lose it as input; an In module's sends go; a plugin module's plug-in goes. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_set
title: Set a module's knobs, label, place or bypass.
description: Set a module's knobs, label, place or bypass. params merge into its knobs (values in the knob's units; a choice by key; a default value is dropped from the file). A knob edit is heard at once, without a recompile. bypass passes each input to the output of its kind. label names it (an Out module's label is what channels' input menus list). preset: a factory preset by name (module.describe lists them): every knob to it, then params on top. See describe for errors and examples.

name: module_write
title: Write a module to the library and compile it; racks use it at once.
description: Write a module to the library and compile it; racks use it at once. name: its library name (lower case, digits, '_' or '-'). source: the whole module, a struct deriving from Module (the module guide; module.get shows any type's source). The file is saved even when it does not compile, so module.edit can fix it; ok and diagnostics (line, column, hint) say how it went. Once it compiles, type describes it as module.describe does and module.add takes its id; modules already playing it are rebuilt with the new code (reloaded counts them), their knobs kept. A version that does not compile leaves racks on the last that did. See describe for errors and examples.

name: plugin_list
title: List scanned plugins; filter matches id, name, or vendor.
description: List scanned plugins; filter matches id, name, or vendor.  See describe for errors and examples.

features.description: CLAP features (a VST3's subcategories): the main category first, then the kind of plugin, such as reverb

shadowed.description: Another location earlier on the plugin path has the same id; fx.add by id uses that one

name: plugin_scan
title: Rescan configured plugin paths and return the available plugins.
description: Rescan configured plugin paths and return the available plugins. wait: false scans in the background (every module through the supervised scanner) and returns at once with the current list and the scan's job; the catalogue changes when the job is done. A background scan already running is returned instead of a second one. See describe for errors and examples.

wait.description: false: scan in the background (default true)

features.description: CLAP features (a VST3's subcategories): the main category first, then the kind of plugin, such as reverb

name: project_get
title: Show the project: name, rate, tempo, meter, file, version and branch.
description: Show the project: name, rate, tempo, meter, file, version and branch. recoverable: recordings a crash left out of the project (project.recoverable). autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file; open it as a project if you want it (nothing is loaded silently). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_open
title: Open a project file (replaces the current project and its history).
description: Open a project file (replaces the current project and its history). recoverable > 0: recordings a crash left out of the project; project.recoverable lists them and project.recover puts them back. autosave_available: a newer autosave exists next to the file (it is not loaded silently). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_recover
title: Put recordings a crash left out back into the project (one undo step).
description: Put recordings a crash left out back into the project (one undo step). files: as project.recoverable lists them (omit for all). Each becomes an item on the track it was recorded on (or track) at the position it was recorded. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_recoverable
title: List recordings a crash left out of the project.
description: List recordings a crash left out of the project. Takes recorded but never committed (the program stopped mid-recording) or never saved, found in the media folder's rec/. start_seconds is where each was recorded; seconds includes audio written after the file's last header update. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_save
title: Save the project (canonical JSON) to its file or a new path.
description: Save the project (canonical JSON) to its file or a new path. path: where to save (becomes the project's file); omit to save in place. warnings: running plug-ins whose current state could not be read; the file keeps the state each had before (fx.restart, then save again, or replace the plug-in). See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_set
title: Change project metadata (name, title, author, notes, Console 9, timebase).
description: Change project metadata (name, title, author, notes, Console 9, timebase). timebase: what items follow when the tempo changes, for items and tracks that inherit it — beats (default), time or beats_position; they keep their place now. See describe for errors and examples.

history_budget_bytes.description: Estimated retained history byte budget; default 1 GiB. Leases and branch boundaries may exceed it.

source.description: The dialog's source; render.mix always renders the mix

masters.description: The mix: the masters to render, a file each (default: tr_0)

pattern.description: File name pattern (session-model §7.3; may contain / for subfolders), for every source or as {mix, stems, regions}

items.title: render output
items.description: One encoding of the rendered audio

bit_depth.description: WAV 16/24/32 (float) [32]; AIFF and FLAC 16/24 [24]; none for MP3 and Vorbis

dither.description: 16- and 24-bit output: none, tpdf (default) or shaped

suffix.description: Inserted before the extension of a second or later output, e.g. "-16bit"

outputs.description: 1-4 encodings of the same audio [[{format: wav, bit_depth: 32}]]

scope.description: file (default), or master: stems share the master mix's gain

seamless_loop.description: Sum the tail into the start (needs tail_s)

handles_s.description: Regions: seconds added at both ends

mode.description: isolated (default; no master processing) or through_master

skip_silent.description: Leave out stems whose peak is below -90 dBFS

metadata.title: render metadata
metadata.description: Tags written into each file; text members accept the file-name tokens

cover.description: A PNG or JPEG of at most 10 MiB, relative to the project folder

bwf.description: WAV: a BWF bext chunk (v2) with time reference and loudness

markers.description: WAV cue points / AIFF markers for the markers and regions in the file's range

name: project_template_delete
title: Delete a saved project template by name.
description: Delete a saved project template by name.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_list
title: List saved project templates by name and path.
description: List saved project templates by name and path.  See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_load
title: Start a new, unsaved project from a project template.
description: Start a new, unsaved project from a project template. Replaces the current project and its history, like project.new: unsaved changes are lost, so save first. The new project has no file until project.save {path} and gets its own copy of the template's audio; the template itself is never changed. See describe for errors and examples.

name: project_template_save
title: Save the whole project as a named project template.
description: Save the whole project as a named project template. Writes the project as it is now (tracks, FX and their states, routing, items, settings; not the history) to a folder of its own in the user's templates directory, with a copy of every audio file it uses. The project keeps its own file. replace: true replaces a template of that name. warnings: running plug-ins whose current state could not be read; the template has the state each had before. See describe for errors and examples.

name: rack_add
title: Add a modular rack on a channel, its Out the input.
description: Add a modular rack on a channel, its Out the input. A rack is a patching space homed on a channel (track, or a new channel named after name). It starts with an Out module, made the channel's input: what the patch sends to Out plays on the channel, before its inserts and Console 9 stage. The channel's MIDI items play into Notes modules. Add modules with module.add and connect them with cable.add. See describe for errors and examples.

description: Set track fields: name, type, volume, pan, mute, solo, polarity, mono, arming. Only the given fields change. solo: off | on | in_place | defeat. armed + record_input (device input channels, 1-based) prepare a track for transport.record; record_midi records MIDI instead: a device name (substring of the MIDI port, "*" = every device) with midi_channel 1-16 (0 = all). monitor: off | on | auto (auto: while armed) — a monitored track hears its input live (an instrument plays the keyboard), also while stopped. record_mode: input (new items), midi_overdub (merge into the MIDI item under the start, as a new take), midi_replace. color: red | orange | yellow | green | teal | blue | violet | grey | "#rrggbb" ("" clears it), shown as a stripe on the track. A master takes armed alone: transport.record then records its output (after its fader, before its own items) as an item on the master; lane_mute silences a master's items. See describe for errors and examples.

channels.description: 1-2: the strip's main pair; up to 128 adds auxiliary channels 3-128 for routes and plug-in pins (a detector on 3/4, a multi-out instrument's outputs), outside the fader, pan and parent send

description: Set or toggle the loop range: playback reaching its end repeats it. start and end as seconds, beat or bar (start_bar 5, end_bar 9 = bars 5-8); a range turns the loop on unless enabled says otherwise; enabled alone toggles the current range; clear removes the range and turns the loop off. name: transport_metronome
title: Turn the metronome on or off and set its level; returns the settings.
description: Turn the metronome on or off and set its level; returns the settings. A click on every beat of the meter while the transport plays (the bar's first accented), in the live output only: renders and recordings never contain it. count_in_bars: that many bars of clicks (at the meter and tempo where playback starts) before transport.record begins — the position holds and nothing is recorded until the count ends; count_in_playback counts in before transport.play too. The count clicks even with the metronome off. Transport state: not an undo step, not saved in the project. No arguments: the current settings. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_playrate_apply-to-tempo
title: Scale every tempo-point BPM by master playrate, then reset the rate to 1.
description: Scale every tempo-point BPM by master playrate, then reset the rate to 1. One version: multiply every BPM by the saved scalar rate, preserving beat positions, ramp flags and meter changes, and reset rate to 1. Require stopped transport, no recording and no active nonempty master playrate envelope. Reject resulting BPM outside 1..1000 before mutation. Existing item timebases still apply; time-locked audio is not made sound-equivalent by this tempo edit. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_playrate_get
title: Get requested/effective master playrate, pitch mode and active envelope.
description: Get requested/effective master playrate, pitch mode and active envelope. requested_rate is the saved project ratio; envelope names the active nonempty tr_0/playrate envelope, including automation items. No engine is required. effective_rate follows consumed output, including compensated source transitions and graph/backend output latency; it is 1.0 without a running engine. GUI clients can use EngineApp::playrateState() without executing/logging a query each sync. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_playrate_set
title: Set the project's master playrate ratio and preserve-pitch flag.
description: Set the project's master playrate ratio and preserve-pitch flag. rate: finite 0.25..4.0 (default 1); preserve_pitch defaults false in a new project. Omitted fields keep their values. Updates during a drag use Origin.gesture like strip faders, and write/touch/latch capture tr_0/playrate coarsely: unlike strip levels (ADR-0061), the curve keeps playing while it is written (no hold or touch return). Recording requires unity. Settings are saved/undoable. File sources convert before take FX and live input mixing; instruments retain their pitch. Scalar edits ramp and converter changes crossfade for 10 ms after priming. Edits include the render horizon and compensated source lookahead; newer requests coalesce while a transition finishes. Long-latency take chains can exceed the usual 200 ms response. effective_rate follows audible output, independently of requested_rate. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_punch
title: Set or toggle the punch range: recordings keep only that range.
description: Set or toggle the punch range: recordings keep only that range. start and end as seconds, beat or bar; a range turns punch on unless enabled says otherwise; clear removes the range and turns punch off. The recording keeps running; the committed items cover only the punch range (the file keeps everything). Not an undo step. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_record
title: Play and record every armed track's input or master's output.
description: Play and record every armed track's input or master's output. Recording requires saved master rate 1 and no active master rate envelope that leaves 1 anywhere, including automation items. Non-unity recording and an armed track with unsupported output record mode are refused before opening files. An armed master records its output (after its fader, before its own items) as an item on the master; while it records, its items are silent in the punch range, or everywhere without punch. See describe for errors and examples.

name: transport_seek
title: Move the play position (one of seconds, beat or bar).
description: Move the play position (one of seconds, beat or bar). With master playrate enabled, prepare file-source converters off-thread before publishing the audible seek. Existing playback and live monitoring continue until ready; preparation errors leave the old seek epoch intact. See describe for errors and examples.
